name: Claim 49

stars.name: Dim Forty-Nine
stars.notes: Cool red dwarf with low luminosity. Entire habitable zone falls within 0.2 AU, leaving the outer system in permanent deep freeze.

planets.name: Scrape
planets.notes: Tidally locked rock orbiting close to the star. Dayside temperatures barely reach habitable range; nightside is perpetually frozen.

planets.name: Frostcut
planets.notes: Ice-sheathed world with subsurface ocean. Automated drills extract water ice and deuterium from the frozen surface for fuel processing.

planets.name: Deepfreeze
planets.notes: Outermost body, a frozen dwarf with nitrogen ice plains. Contains pockets of rare cryogenic compounds valued in industrial chemistry.

anomalies.name: The Cold Spot
anomalies.notes: A region of space measurably colder than surrounding vacuum by 0.3 Kelvin. Cause unknown. Ice crystals form spontaneously on ship hulls passing through.

asteroid_belts.name: Frostfield
asteroid_belts.notes: Belt of ice-encrusted rocks containing frozen volatiles, water ice, and ammonia compounds. Primary target for ice mining drones.

stations.name: Claim 49 Processing Hub
stations.notes: Small automated ice processing facility with minimal crew. Converts raw ice into deuterium pellets and purified water for export.

faction_control.notes: Low-value system operated as one of dozens of ice mining claims by the Consortium. Minimal oversight, minimal investment.

history: Cataloged in 2534 as the 49th mining claim filed by the Glacial Rift Ice Consortium during their expansion into the outer sectors.
Automated extraction began in 2537; the system has operated continuously since with only periodic crewed maintenance visits.
The Cold Spot anomaly was first documented in 2551 by a supply freighter crew who reported ice forming inside their cargo bay while transiting the region.
description: Claim 49 is exactly what its name suggests: a numbered stake in the cold dark, one of dozens operated by the Glacial Rift Ice Consortium across the outer sectors. Three frozen worlds huddle around a dim red dwarf whose meager light barely warms the innermost planet above freezing. The system exists for one purpose--ice extraction--and every piece of infrastructure reflects that singular focus. There is nothing here that does not serve the harvest.

Frostcut is the primary target, its ice sheets kilometers thick and rich in deuterium that fuels fusion reactors across the sector. Automated drills bore through the frozen surface, extracting cylinders of ice that are shuttled to the orbital processing hub for refinement. The Frostfield belt supplements this with smaller-scale comet harvesting. Output is steady if unspectacular--Claim 49 will never make anyone rich, but it reliably supplies the fuel that keeps civilization running in the outer sectors.

The Cold Spot between Frostcut and Deepfreeze is the system's only point of scientific interest. The anomalous temperature depression defies easy explanation, and the spontaneous ice crystal formation it causes has damaged sensitive equipment on passing ships. The Consortium considers it a navigational nuisance; a few academic researchers have petitioned for study access but been denied on liability grounds. Crews passing through Claim 49 speak of the place with the resigned familiarity of long-haul truckers--it is cold, it is lonely, and the ice never stops flowing.
